stem: A manufacturer with 15 accounts in AWS Organizations wants employees to sign in to all accounts with their existing on-premises Active Directory credentials. Passwords must stay on premises, and the company will not run any domain controllers in AWS. Which TWO components should the solutions architect use? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: A Simple AD directory that is populated with copies of the employee accounts
An Amazon Cognito user pool that imports the employee accounts from Active Directory
AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a two-way forest trust to the on-premises domain
AD Connector in the management account, pointing to the on-premises domain
IAM Identity Center using that directory as its identity source, with permission sets per account

rationale: AD Connector is a directory gateway that redirects requests to the on-premises Active Directory without caching any information in the cloud and without domain controllers in AWS. IAM Identity Center can use an AD Connector in the management account as its identity source, performs pass-through authentication so no passwords are synchronized, and grants AD groups access to accounts through permission sets. Simple AD is a standalone Samba-based directory that is closed to new customers, does not support trusts, and is not supported by IAM Identity Center. A Cognito user pool is a directory for users of your web and mobile apps and would hold its own copies of the users. AWS Managed Microsoft AD creates a pair of domain controllers in your VPC, which the company has ruled out.
